purpose: Regression cases for the versioned ASHRAE thermodynamic wet-bulb method using IAPWS-IF97 liquid-water saturation pressure. These cases are analytical software checks, not engineering approval.

ashrae_fundamentals_f25_ch1_iapws.title: ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals (2025), Chapter 1: Psychrometrics, Equations 5, 21, 26, 30 and 33
ashrae_fundamentals_f25_ch1_iapws.supports: Pure-water saturation pressure above freezing from IAPWS-IF97 and thermodynamic wet-bulb humidity-ratio, enthalpy and specific-volume relationships under perfect-gas assumptions.

cases.equation: ASHRAE Fundamentals F25 Eq. 5, IAPWS-IF97 Region 4: theta = T + n9/(T-n10), A=theta^2+n1 theta+n2, B=n3 theta^2+n4 theta+n5, C=n6 theta^2+n7 theta+n8, pws=[2C/(-B+sqrt(B^2-4AC))]^4 MPa; convert MPa to kPa.
assumptions: Pure-water saturation pressure is used in the perfect-gas psychrometric relation; saturated moist-air enhancement factor is omitted as in the cited perfect-gas equations.

cases.equation: ASHRAE Fundamentals F25 Eqs. 5, 21, 33, 26, and 30; dry-air mass flow is volumetric flow divided by outdoor specific volume; sensible load uses cp_da=1.006 kJ/(kg_da K), latent is total less sensible.
assumptions: Values independently evaluated from fixed published equations and then rounded to the project's four-decimal kW result precision.

cases.equation: Use Eq. 5 to convert dew point to water-vapour pressure, Eq. 21 for humidity ratio, then solve Eqs. 5, 21 and 33 for the thermodynamic wet-bulb temperature by bisection.
assumptions: Dew point is at or above 0°C and no higher than dry bulb; liquid-water saturation and perfect-gas psychrometric equations apply.
exclusions: Sub-zero dew points requiring saturation over ice
